- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (especially > -0.5) — model tends to ignore downside risk.
- Underestimate sharp downward moves after recent spikes — model fails to capture momentum reversal.
- Overreact to short-term sentiment swings — forecasts overshoot when sentiment shifts sharply (e.g., +0.37 to -0.53).
- Exhibit mean reversion bias — model overcorrects after strong upward moves, then undercorrects downward.
- Lag in response to sentiment — model reacts to sentiment changes with 1–2 days delay, especially for negative sentiment.
- Forecast horizon 30d is overly optimistic — consistently overestimates early in the period, then underestimates late.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model still overestimates — fails to account for risk aversion or policy uncertainty.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends — if last 3–5 days show strong decline, model often ignores it and forecasts upward.
